household: with her humans, Sue and Mike
work: The Book of Night with Moon
creator: Diane Duane
address_as_given: an apartment on the upper East Side of New York's Manhattan Island
notes: Rhiow, a black cat and leader of a team of feline wizards who keep the Grand Central worldgates running, lives with her owners in an apartment with a terrace. No street or building is given in the sources found; the point is the neighborhood centroid. The book is set in the present day of the Young Wizards series, between books four and five.
source_quote: To her owners, apartment-dwellers on the upper East Side of New York's Manhattan Island, Rhiow looks like nothing more than their little black pet cat

household: about 150 talking dogs, among them the historian Ludwig von Sacher
creator: Kirsten Bakis
notes: On arriving in New York in 2008 after their Canadian settlement of Rankstadt is destroyed, the dogs take rooms at the Plaza Hotel before building their own castle on the Lower East Side. The Plaza survives at Fifth Avenue and Central Park South.
source_quote: they are forced to move in the year 2008 to New York (where 150 of them take up residence at the Plaza Hotel) when Rankstadt is destroyed.

household: the dog community, among them the historian Ludwig von Sacher
creator: Kirsten Bakis
address_as_given: an enormous Bavarian castle on the Lower East Side
notes: The dogs' second home, a castle they build themselves soon after arriving; the review gives only the neighborhood, so the point is a Lower East Side centroid. The setting years after 2008 are an estimate.
source_quote: shortly after their arrival they construct an enormous Bavarian castle on the Lower East Side.

creator: Hubert Selby Jr.
notes: Bobby is a 13-year-old boy whose plans with his girlfriend Maria are shattered by a gang attack. No street is given in the source; the point is in Mott Haven, at the core of the South Bronx. Setting year is an estimate from the publication date.
source_quote: The protagonist is a thirteen-year-old African-American boy named Bobby who lives in an apartment in South Bronx with his mother and siblings.

creator: Cheryl Mendelson
address_as_given: a sedate old apartment building in Morningside Heights
notes: The Braithwaites, an opera singer and a pianist, moved to the Heights in the early 1980s; the novel is set in 1999. Their late neighbor across the hall, 103-year-old Elizabeth Miller, drives the plot. A search snippet gave 635 West 117th Street for the building, but no page I could open confirmed it, so it is not used. Novel first published 2003 (the list gives 1999).
source_quote: Anne and Charles Braithwaite have spent their entire married life in a sedate old apartment building in Morningside Heights
source2_quote: When Anne and Charles Braithwaite moved to the Heights in the early ’80s it was a great place to live: adjacent to Columbia University

household: with her boyfriend, later fiance, Luke Brandon
creator: Sophie Kinsella
notes: Becky and Luke share an apartment in the West Village while she works as a personal shopper at Barneys. No street was found in an openable source. Setting years are estimated from publication.
source_quote: The book opens with Becky living with her boyfriend Luke in Manhattan's West Village.

character: Maggie Sowle and the residents of Echo Terrace
household: residents including a quilter, an undertaker and an ex-Luftwaffe pilot, with concierge Farro Fescu
creator: Nicholas Rinaldi
address_as_given: Echo Terrace, a glitzy condo close by the Twin Towers
notes: An invented condominium in Battery Park City near the World Trade Center; the story runs from 1992 through the 1993 bombing to September 2001. Kirkus and the Virginia Quarterly Review call the building Echo Terrace, while Wikipedia calls it Echo Park; Echo Terrace is used here.
source_quote: Echo Terrace, a glitzy condo close by the Twin Towers, is aptly named, for the building is clamorous with ghosts as the story begins in 1992.
source2_quote: residents of Echo Park, a fictitious Battery Park condominium and its Romanian concierge, Farro Fescu.

household: her parents' home, left to her alone for the summer
creator: Truman Capote
notes: The publisher places the McNeils in a Fifth Avenue penthouse with no number or cross street. One unverified summary says it overlooks the park, so the point sits on Fifth Avenue along Central Park, with a wide radius. Written in the 1940s, published posthumously in 2005.
source_quote: follows a carefree young socialite, Grady McNeil, whose parents leave her alone in their Fifth Avenue penthouse for the summer.

creator: Paul Auster
notes: Orr, a novelist recovering from a near-fatal illness, lives with his wife in Cobble Hill; the novel is set in September 1982. No street was confirmed in an openable source, so the point is the neighborhood centroid.
source_quote: Sidney lives in Cobble Hill with his wife Grace Tebbetts, a book designer he adores.
